This appeal under Section 101 of the Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (in short, "the Act") by the appellant-petitioner is directed against the impugned order dated 16.09.2025 passed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge-cum-special Judge, Children's Court,
Nabarangpur in CT Case No. 3/2025(JV) (Arising out of JC Case No. 06 of 2025) corresponding to Tentulikhunti PS Case No. 10 of 2025 refusing to grant bail to Child-in-Conflict with law (CICL) who is represented by his legal guardian (Paternal Uncle) in this criminal appeal for commission of offence punishable U/Ss. 363/366/376(2)(n)/313/ 323/294/506/342/34 IPC, on the main allegation of committing rape upon the victim.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard, Mr. Sabyasachi Mishra, learned counsel for the appellant-petitioner and Mr. P.Satapathy,
learned Addl. PP in the matter and perused the record.
3.

Bail to the CICL can only be refused if there exists reasonable materials for believing that the release of the child-in-conflict with law (CICL) would bring him into association with any known criminal or expose him to moral, physical or psychological danger or his release would defeats the ends of justice, but no such situation is prevailing in this case.

In the aforesaid backdrop and taking into account the nature and gravity of the offences as alleged against the CICL vis- -vis the accusation sought to be brought against him and regard being had to the detention of the CICL in observation home since 19.01.2025 and keeping in view the other circumstance on record in entirety including the statement of the victim and the inherent right of the CICL to be presumed innocent until proven guilty at the trial and no criminal antecedent of similar nature being reported against the appellant, this Court without expressing any opinion on merit, considers it proper to admit the appellant to bail.
4. Hence, the Criminal Appeal stands allowed and the impugned order is hereby set aside.
Consequently, the appellant be released on bail on such terms and conditions as deems fit and proper by the learned Court in seisin of the case.
